Tavi wanted to be included in a surprise. Then Mina opened the little wooden tube.

Mina opened the wooden tube and read the label aloud. “This hello is for Grandma!” she said, blinking at the unexpected name.

Mina chose the golden scrap and fastened it into a long tail. “A steady tail for a steady hello,” she said.

Mina found Pip beside the worktable. “The tube says Grandma,” she told him. Pip’s little smoke-puff curled into a question mark.

Mina placed the tube in Pip’s careful claws. “Keep it safe and keep the flight gentle.” Pip tucked it close, as if it were a sleeping beetle.

Pip glanced at the tube, then at Mina’s careful tail. “I can fly quietly,” he said. “Quietly can still be splendid.” His smoke puff became a tiny silver star.

The kite rose in a calm little arc. Pip held the tube close while Mina guided the string, and the paper tail traced a neat blue-gold-red smile across the sky.

Mina ran three steps and released the kite. Up it climbed, tugging the spool toward the bright blue sky.

The smooth kite settled beside Grandma, its paper tail fluttering like a tiny flag. Pip’s quiet hello had arrived without waking a single sleeping pigeon.
